interest: This document is of archival and historical interest as an illustration of U.S. State Department filing, cross-referencing, and indexing practices during and immediately after World War II. It highlights the wartime displacement of American diplomatic and consular personnel, specifically Walter A. Foote representing the Batavia consulate while based in Melbourne following the fall of the Netherlands East Indies. Additionally, it provides a valuable lead for researchers studying Japanese wartime psychological warfare, espionage, and propaganda campaigns targeted at Australia in the Pacific theater by directing them to decimal file 894.2020/6.
overview: This file (894.20247) consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing records under the subject 'Military Activities of Japan in Australia.' The sheet indexes document sub-number 4, an October 26 communication (despatch No. 4) originating from U.S. diplomat Walter A. Foote, designated as Batavia at Melbourne, which transmitted a survey of Japanese propaganda directed toward Australia. The notation cross-references the substantive survey to decimal file 894.2020/6, preserving an administrative record of Japanese intelligence and propaganda monitoring within this classification.

subfiles.summary: This single-page Department of State List of Papers control sheet (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, covers records under decimal classification 894.20247 concerning Japanese military activities in Australia. It indexes sub-number 4, an October 26 communication sent by Walter A. Foote (designated Batavia at Melbourne, despatch No. 4) transmitting a survey of Japanese propaganda directed at Australia. The purport directs researchers to decimal file 894.2020/6, indicating that the substantive enclosure was transferred or filed under that related classification.
